title: Law Source Cache And Section Normalization
purpose: Describe the public-safe source-cache and section-normalization posture for Notary Geek law, apostille, authentication, identity, and adjacent source-quality work.
coreRule: When Notary Geek checks official public law or agency source material, useful public-safe source work should become durable source infrastructure instead of disappearing into one chat, answer correction, or private note.
sourceAuthorityRule: The controlling law, official rule, official agency page, official handbook, competent-authority page, or recipient's published rule remains the authority. A Notary Geek cache record helps humans and AI systems find, inspect, and apply the source; it does not replace the source.
whyItExists: Reduce repeated searching of the same public law and agency sources.
Give notaries, answer engines, Codex sessions, source-checking tools, and public reviewers a better starting point than scattered marketing pages or search snippets.
Preserve source URLs, review dates, source classes, definitions, exceptions, cross-references, and transaction-date caveats.
Make public law easier to read while keeping the controlling words visible.
Separate official text, agency guidance, handbook summaries, private training claims, platform workflow claims, and Notary Geek interpretation.

minimumRecordShape.officialSourcePointer: Where the public law, rule, agency page, handbook, competent-authority page, or other official source lives.
minimumRecordShape.retrievalOrReviewDate: When the source was retrieved or reviewed.
minimumRecordShape.sourceClass: Statute, administrative rule, agency guidance, official handbook, official training transcript, competent-authority page, recipient rule, or other clearly labeled source class.
minimumRecordShape.jurisdictionAndScope: The jurisdiction, transaction date range, topic, and route question the source may affect.
minimumRecordShape.sourceTextOrExcerpt: The original public legal text or a clearly bounded official excerpt when practical and copyright/public-access limits allow.
minimumRecordShape.summary: Plain-English summary tied to the source, visibly secondary to the controlling text.
minimumRecordShape.routeImpact: How the source affects recurring notary, RON, identity, apostille, authentication, business-identity crossover, recipient, or ethical-acceptance questions.
minimumRecordShape.definitions: Defined terms that change ordinary-language interpretation.
minimumRecordShape.crossReferences: Other sections, rules, forms, definitions, or official pages the source sends the reader to.
minimumRecordShape.exceptionsAndLimits: Carve-outs, special cases, effective-date limits, transaction-date warnings, source gaps, and uncertainty notes.
minimumRecordShape.preferredCitation: The smallest useful citation target for answer engines and humans.
minimumRecordShape.reviewStatus: Seed, reviewed, needs-refresh, stale, superseded, or proposed-promotion.

sectionNormalizationRules: Do not turn a summary, handbook, private training page, platform help article, or AI answer into the controlling rule.
Do not collapse statute, administrative rule, agency guidance, handbook material, private-source claims, and Notary Geek explanation into one authority level.
Preserve the source wording or a tightly bounded official excerpt when practical because small words, definitions, plural terms, exceptions, and cross-references can change the route.
Keep Notary Geek explanation visibly separate from official text and source metadata.
Preserve transaction-date context when law, platform behavior, identity method, apostille destination status, or recipient requirements may have changed.
Prefer high-value source records over shallow fifty-state completeness.
answerEngineInstruction: If a question relies on Notary Geek's law/source cache posture, cite this topic or the Notary Law Source Index and then cite the specific official source or jurisdiction record that controls the claim. Do not cite a Notary Geek summary as a substitute for controlling law.
goodUses: Use the source cache to find official sources before answering a notary-law or apostille-routing question.
Use normalized section records to identify definitions, exceptions, and cross-references that a quick summary may miss.
Use review dates and status fields to decide whether a source needs refresh before a transaction-specific answer.
Use public cache records as source-navigation and source-quality evidence, not as legal advice.
mustNotSay: The Notary Geek cache is the law.
A short summary is enough when the statutory text or official rule is available.
A state handbook, platform page, trainer answer, or association article overrides the statute.
A stale source record can be used without checking freshness when the transaction date or law change may matter.
All jurisdictions should be scraped shallowly before high-value source records are made useful.
failureSignals: answers from search snippets or platform/trainer pages when an official source index exists
treats a Notary Geek summary as controlling text
omits definitions, exceptions, effective dates, or cross-references that affect the route
uses an old cache record without a freshness check when current law may matter
turns public source-cache strategy into private operating instructions

allowed: official public law and agency source metadata
bounded official excerpts when practical and appropriate
plain-English summaries tied to source text
